title: Console prune & operational canvas — sprint cutlist (Mar 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working cutlist / pruning canvas for the Console & Rollouts backlog ahead of Sprint 27 (mid-Mar–Apr 2026 cadence). Goal: reduce sprint scope to a focused set of tasks that protect the critical rollout observability work while deferring lower-value UI polish and exploratory spikes. Treat this as an operational prioritization artifact — decisions here should drive the sprint board and the canary runway schedule.

Quick summary decisions (TL;DR):
- Keep: CON-2142 (rollout fallback metrics) — high business risk if not shipped.
- Keep (reduced scope): CON-2176 (per-route trace links) — move heavy graphing to follow-up; deliver light linking + sampling.
- Defer: CON-2199 (console theming overhaul) — nice-to-have, no customer blocking.
- Defer: CON-2203 (interactive onboarding tour) — postpone until post-sprint monitor window.
- Spike -> timebox: CON-2231 (native embedding visualizer) — 2d spike only; no UI commit beyond prototype.

Triage heuristics we used (applied in order):
1) Customer blocking / contractual SLA risk (auto-keep).
2) Enables-redwood-dedicated or Private launches (keep if launch path dependent).
3) Observability & rollback safety (favor keep).
4) Estimated dev cost vs. measurable impact in 2-week sprint.
5) Cross-team unblocker value (requests from SRE / infra).

Capacity math (engineering headcount):
- Available devs for console: 3 full-time (Aisha, Ben, María) + 0.6 SRE support (Omar)
- Sprint velocity baseline (avg): ~18 story points for this group
- Reserve for incidents / on-call: 20% of capacity -> target planning capacity = 14 SP

Sprint cutlist (final prioritized list, ordered):
1) CON-2142 | Rollout fallback telemetry & alerting | KEEP | 8 SP | Owner: Ben
   - What: Add fallback detection metrics, route-level success ratio, alert on >3% fallback by 5m window.
   - Why: Prevent outages during model variant rollouts; internal SEV risk if absent.
   - Acceptance: dashboard shows traffic by route + fallback count; PagerDuty runbook updated.

2) CON-2176 | Per-route trace linking (light) | REDUCE-SCOPE | 5 SP | Owner: Aisha
   - What: Add trace link column in request table that opens trace view for sampled requests. Defer full flame-graph view to sprint+1.
   - Why: Observability for rollouts, quick debugging for SEs.
   - Acceptance: Link present and resolves to trace; sampling set to 1% initially.

3) CON-2231 | Embedding visualizer spike | SPIKE-2D | 1 SP | Owner: María
   - What: Prototype small interactive visualization for embedding clusters (local mock dataset). No shipping to prod.
   - Why: Informs UX approach for Optimize product integration.
   - Acceptance: Prototype + 30m demo; notes captured in Confluence.

4) CON-2205 | Route-level batching config UI (small) | KEEP-MINIMUM | 4 SP | Owner: Ben
   - What: Add UI to set batch window (ms) per route and a toggle for KV-cache enabled. Minimal validation only.
   - Why: Immediate cost control lever for customers; used in two existing enterprise pilots.
   - Acceptance: Config persists via API and shows current active value in route detail.

5) CON-2199 | Console theming overhaul | DEFER | 0 SP | Owner: Design backlog
   - What: Full visual refresh (deferred).
   - Why: Low immediate value versus risk.

6) CON-2203 | Interactive onboarding tour | DEFER | 0 SP | Owner: Product growth
   - What: Rich guided onboarding; postpone until we collect post-rollout behavior metrics.

Buffer: 1 SP left for hotfix/incident.

UX / Wireframe callouts (quick notes for dev + design handoff):
- Rollout fallback metrics (CON-2142): give a compact summary card that fits inside existing rollout detail pane. If space-constrained, move link to a slide-over. Priority: legible numbers, not pretty.
- Per-route trace linking (CON-2176): add a tiny link icon in the request table row. Hover tooltip: "Open sampled trace". On click, route to existing trace viewer route /trace/:id (reuse). We must avoid creating a new full-page flow.
- Batching config (CON-2205): inline numeric input (ms) with up/down arrows and an 'Apply' button. Add micro-copy: "Batching trades latency for throughput — typical values 0–200ms."

Unresolved questions / Notes-to-self:
- Sampling rate for traces: default 1% seems fine but confirm with SRE (Omar) about storage cost. Action: Omar to confirm by 2026-03-04.
- Pager duty on fallback alerts: should we auto-escalate to infra-owner? Quick sync with SRE required.
- Does Dedicated sales need any telemetry fields for compliance? Need to check with Solutions Eng.

Risk log (short):
- If CON-2176 scope creeps to full flame-graph integration, we blow the sprint. Mitigation: explicit acceptance criteria and cut point at the trace link.
- CON-2142 requires coordination with infra to expose metrics; delay here would block whole keep. Reserve daily 30m sync until metrics are visible.

Communication plan (who to tell and how):
- Customer Success: email summary + ask for any immediate blockers (Ben)
- SRE: sync meeting Wed 10:30 (Omar) to lock sampling + metric exposures
- Sales / Solutions Eng: brief update in weekly rollout sync on Friday

Follow-ups (action items):
- Ben: open CON-2142 subtask for PD runbook update (by 2026-03-03)
- Aisha: finalize reduced-scope Jira description for CON-2176 and attach wireframe (by 2026-03-04)
- María: run the 2d spike, capture prototype, and schedule demo (by 2026-03-08)
- Omar: confirm trace sampling storage delta and escalation rules (by 2026-03-04)

Appendix: tickets considered and rationale for deferral:
- CON-2210 (full rollout analytics dashboard): deferred because it requires backend aggregation work that would ripple multiple squads; keep as Q2 spike instead.
- CON-2183 (bulk-edit for routes): deferred — too many UX unknowns for this sprint.

Wireframe links (working):
- Confluence: console/operational-canvas -> contains rough Figma embeds and screenshots
- Figma: (internal) figma://file/console-prune-canvas (designers have access)

End-of-doc quick notes: this is intentionally terse and action-oriented. Use this doc to cut the board. If you want to re-open any deferred item, flag in the retrospective with supporting customer signals.

-- Aisha
